package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised via a supply chain attack after an employee's npm credentials were phished. Malicious versions were published that either directly embedded a crypto drainer (1.1.7) or downloaded a secondary malicious package (1.1.5, 1.1.6). The malware presents fake wallet connection prompts and, upon user interaction, drains cryptocurrency assets to attacker-controlled wallets.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user interaction with wallet connection modal)
execution_context.file_location: main application code (likely index.js or bundled source in @ledgerhq/connect-kit v1.1.7)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Displays a fake modal prompt to the user, inviting them to connect their crypto wallet. Upon user interaction, initiates unauthorized transactions to transfer assets from the user's wallet to attacker-controlled addresses.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code creates a deceptive UI to trick users into connecting their wallets and then performs unauthorized transactions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate wallet connector should only facilitate secure, user-authorized transactions and never initiate transfers without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate wallet connectors display modals for user authentication, but never perform hidden or unauthorized transactions.
key_indicators: Fake modal UI mimicking legitimate wallet connection
Automated transaction initiation after user interaction
No user consent for asset transfer

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (upon package initialization in v1.1.5 and v1.1.6)
execution_context.file_location: main application code (likely index.js or bundled source in @ledgerhq/connect-kit v1.1.5/v1.1.6)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a secondary npm package (2e6d5f64604be31) that acts as a crypto drainer, enabling further malicious activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code fetches and executes an unvetted, non-standard package at runtime, which is a common technique for evading static analysis and delivering malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not download or execute arbitrary code from external sources during initialization.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic imports are used in some legitimate plugin systems, but only from trusted, vetted sources.
key_indicators: Dynamic import of a non-standard, obfuscated package
No legitimate dependency or documentation for the secondary package

behavioral_signatures: Display of wallet connection modals not matching legitimate UI patterns
Automated or hidden transaction requests following wallet connection
Dynamic import or execution of non-standard npm packages at runtime
file_indicators: Presence of @ledgerhq/connect-kit versions 1.1.5, 1.1.6, or 1.1.7 in package.json or node_modules
Reference to or presence of npm package 2e6d5f64604be31
network_indicators: Outbound transactions to known attacker-controlled wallet addresses
Unexpected network requests following wallet connection events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the installation or presence of @ledgerhq/connect-kit versions 1.1.5, 1.1.6, or 1.1.7. Flag any dynamic imports or runtime downloads of unlisted npm packages (such as 2e6d5f64604be31). Watch for UI elements that mimic wallet connection prompts but are not part of the legitimate library. Audit for unauthorized or automated crypto transactions initiated immediately after wallet connection events. Correlate with known malicious wallet addresses and monitor for suspicious outbound network activity.
